message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong for not hosting Thanksgiving like I planned to. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, for about 50 years, my mom has been hosting Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her children and grandchildren. That's a long-standing tradition, and it means a lot to everyone involved. Now, my mom is getting too old to keep doing this, so she asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are four of us, and we're rotating who hosts each holiday. So far, each of us has hosted one holiday. This Thanksgiving is my turn. But here's the thing: my wife's family is spread out all over the country, and we've never spent Thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with them. We've just never been as close to them, I guess. But this year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. At first, it was just a sister's trip, but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because she thinks it's a "once in a lifetime event," and I agree with her. Plus, I want to go too. As soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to see what we should do about Thanksgiving because I can't host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though she's up next for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also said, "Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to NYC" and went on about how sad mom will be that I'm doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer up solutions. I also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I said me and him could maybe just swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I have a long-standing family tradition that I agreed to take over when my mom couldn't anymore. It's important to keep that going, especially since it's been a part of our family for so long. On the other hand, this trip to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade with my wife's family seems like a unique opportunity that we all want to take advantage of. It's not every day that you get to go to such a big event with extended family. I also feel like I'm being considerate by trying to offer solutions, like paying for a catered event or swapping with my brother. But my sister is really upset, and she feels like I'm abandoning the tradition that our mom worked so hard to maintain. She even said that Mom wouldn't do this, which makes me feel guilty because I don't want to let Mom down. Maybe I should think about what's more important: keeping the family tradition alive or creating new memories with my wife's family. Both are important, but I'm not sure how to balance them. I also wonder if there's a way to compromise, like hosting a smaller gathering or finding another way to celebrate Thanksgiving that still honors the tradition but also allows us to spend time with my wife's family. I also need to consider how my actions affect my siblings. My oldest sister is really upset, and my brother doesn't seem too happy about the idea of hosting either. It's putting a lot of pressure on them, and I don't want to be the one causing family tension. But at the same time, I feel like I'm missing out on something important with my wife's family. Maybe I should talk to my siblings again and see if there's a way to make this work for everyone. Or perhaps I need to have a heart-to-heart with my wife about our priorities and how we can balance family traditions with new opportunities. It's a tough spot to be in, and I'm not sure what the right decision is.
